plan.title: Mouse liver HFD vs chow DE + Hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 mouse liver samples (6 HFD-treated vs 6 chow-control, unpaired, single batch, raw salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes) are analyzed for differential expression and pathway-level change. Sample sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which per the sourced QC rule must be inspected on PCA/sample-distance plots and reported rather than silently dropped or silently kept — DESeq2's size-factor normalization accounts for depth differences, so removal (if any) is a judgment call made after inspection, not a default. The workflow: (1) sample-structure QC with blinded VST, PCA, and sample-distance heatmap to place sample_01 in context; (2) minimal low-count pre-filtering; (3) DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization and Wald test with an explicit reference level (chow) and contrast (HFD vs chow), apeglm shrinkage of log2 fold changes, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05 to call significant genes; (4) fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic against the MSigDB mouse Hallmark gene set collection (the correct mouse-native collection, not a human set mapped over) to identify hallmark pathways shifting between diet groups; (5) an integrated report with fit diagnostics, gene tables (shrunken and unshrunken LFC), leading-edge genes per significant hallmark set, and a full reproducibility record (package versions, seed, collection version).

design ~ condition, explicit reference level = chow, contrast HFD vs chow
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB mouse Hallmark
DE + enrichment report with QC, diagnostics, leading edge, reproducibility record
